correctness.rationale: For B_q with words (a,b) and directed E((a,b),(c,d)) iff b=c, a single-variable atomic type recognizes q=1 versus q≥2; a two-variable formula separates q=2 from q≥3, and the full two-pebble local response table uses only three letters and proves permanent equivalence for any q,q′≥3. For k≥3, the three-variable formulas ∃z(E(z,x)∧E(z,y)) and ∃z(E(x,z)∧E(y,z)) encode equality of first/second coordinates. By locally shadowing a third variable only inside a conjunct, k word-variables can describe all equality patterns of up to 2k alphabet positions, including an odd t with a final diagonal word, yielding separating sentences for thresholds t≤2k. Duplicator maintains the complete equality pattern of all coordinates of ≤k pebbled words for q,q′≥2k since replacing one word needs ≤2 fresh letters. Thus cutoffs are 2,3,2k and the stated distinguishing-width law follows. These are unbounded-round strategies, not finite-depth experimental extrapolation.
residual_risks: The result assumes counting-free FO^k and loops in pure directed adjacency; a richer language changes cutoffs.

value.rationale: The pure adjacency length-two de Bruijn graph is a canonical automata/network structure with q² vertices. The exact classification of all finite-variable theories, the anomalous two-variable plateau and the constructive minimal separating width provide a complete natural model-theoretic invariant, illustrating sharp expressivity costs of definable coordinates.
residual_risks: Other word lengths, Kautz graphs and counting logic may have distinct thresholds; result does not pretend to classify them.

limitations: Only positive q and counting-free FO^k over the single directed adjacency relation with loops.
Possible unindexed general incidence-interpretation theorem is a qualified originality risk.
